messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Social behaviour and attitudes, Media, Political behaviour and attitudes, Government, political systems and organisations, Elections, Economic policy, public expenditure and revenue, and Economic systems and development in Germany during the 2010s, matching this research need: German election campaign survey data on political attitudes, vote intention and behavior, party and candidate evaluations, issue positions, media use, social networks, trust, economic perceptions, and detailed demographics around the 2013 federal/state elections
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS GLES 2013 campaign panel study federal election 2013 dataset DOI
GLES 2013 rolling cross section campaign media use candidate evaluations dataset
German Longitudinal Election Study 2013 state elections campaign survey dataset GESIS
action.query: GESIS GLES 2013 campaign panel study federal election 2013 dataset DOI

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Rolling Cross-Section Campaign Survey with Post-election Panel Wave (GLES 2013)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.13214","justification":"Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset for the research need. Part of the German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), this survey examines political attitudes, voting intentions, electoral behavior, party and candidate evaluations, political issues, media consumption, interpersonal political communication, economic perceptions, and sociodemographic characteristics surrounding the 2013 German federal election. Data were collected between July 8 and November 3, 2013, using computer-assisted telephone interviews. Its rolling cross-sectional design permits daily analysis of campaign dynamics, while the post-election panel wave supports investigation of changes in political preferences and actual voting behavior. GESIS study ZA5703, version 2.0.2."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Election Campaign Panel 2013","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/data-and-documentation","justification":"Highly relevant longitudinal survey of eligible German voters during the 2013 federal election campaign. The election campaign panel is designed to investigate changes in political attitudes, party preferences, vote intentions, candidate evaluations, issue positions, and campaign engagement across successive survey waves. Particularly valuable for studying individual-level changes in political behavior, campaign effects, media exposure, political discussions, and the relationship between economic perceptions and electoral decisions. The GESIS landing page provides access to the GLES study collection and documentation."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Cross-Section Pre-Election and Post-Election Surveys 2013","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/data-and-documentation","justification":"Strong match for analyzing voter attitudes and behavior before and after the September 2013 German federal election. The GLES cross-sectional surveys provide information on electoral participation, voting decisions, political interest, party identification, candidate perceptions, issue priorities, political trust, economic evaluations, and demographic characteristics. The pre-election and post-election structure facilitates comparisons between stated voting intentions and reported electoral behavior. The post-election study also contributes to the German component of the Comparative Study of Electoral Systems (CSES)."},{"title":"Candidate Campaign Survey 2013, Survey and Electoral/Structural Data (GLES)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.12043","justification":"Directly relevant supplementary dataset examining political attitudes, campaign activities, political communication, and issue positions among candidates participating in the 2013 German federal election. The survey covers candidates from CDU, CSU, SPD, FDP, Alliance 90/The Greens, and Die Linke. Data collection took place between October 16, 2013, and January 10, 2014. The dataset combines candidate survey responses with electoral and structural information, enabling comparisons between candidate positions, party strategies, and voter preferences. Particularly valuable for research on political representation, campaign organization, party competition, and candidate behavior. GESIS study ZA5716."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study 2013 – Short-term Campaign Panel Control Group II","url_or_doi":"https://access.gesis.org/dbk/55127","justification":"Relevant supplementary dataset from the GLES 2013 election campaign research program. This online panel survey covers individuals eligible to vote in the 2013 German Bundestag election. It provides a comparison group for the short-term campaign panel, supporting research on changes in political attitudes and electoral preferences across the campaign period. Particularly useful for investigating campaign effects and assessing differences between repeated survey participants and comparison-group respondents. The GESIS documentation identifies the study as the second control group associated with the 2013 short-term campaign panel."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study 2013 – Long-term Panel and Election Campaign Panel Intermediate Survey","url_or_doi":"https://access.gesis.org/dbk/58020","justification":"Relevant longitudinal survey resource linking the GLES 2013 long-term panel and election campaign panel. It is useful for studying political attitudes and electoral preferences in the context of the 2013 federal election and for examining continuity and change in political orientations across survey periods. The intermediate survey provides additional observations for researchers investigating the relationship between longer-term political predispositions and short-term election campaign dynamics. GESIS documentation identifies the study as the 2013 intermediate survey of the long-term and election campaign panels."},{"title":"Long-term Online Tracking Survey for the 2013 Bavarian State Election (GLES)","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/elections/german-state-elections","justification":"Strong supplementary match for the state-election component of the research need. This GLES study focuses on the 2013 Bavarian state election, which occurred shortly before the September 2013 federal election. The online tracking design is relevant for examining electoral preferences and political attitudes in a regional campaign context. It can support comparisons between federal and state electoral dynamics, especially regarding party competition and voter decision-making. Listed by GESIS under study number ZA5736, the dataset is particularly useful for investigating the interaction between regional and national electoral politics."},{"title":"Quick Survey on the Federal Parliament Election 2013 (Blitzumfrage zur Bundestagswahl 2013)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA5937?lang=en","justification":"Relevant supplementary survey specifically focused on the 2013 German federal election. The dataset belongs to the GESIS collection of election-related research data and is classified under political behavior and attitudes, government and political systems, and elections. It provides an additional election-specific survey source for studying political opinions and electoral behavior around the 2013 Bundestag election. Particularly useful for supplementing the more extensive GLES panel and cross-sectional studies. GESIS study ZA5937."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Election Studies and Campaign Research Data Collection","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/data-and-documentation","justification":"Authoritative landing page for the broader collection of German election research datasets, including the 2013 federal election studies. The collection encompasses rolling cross-sectional campaign surveys, election campaign panels, long-term panels, pre-election and post-election cross-sections, candidate studies, and other election-related research components. It is especially useful for identifying complementary datasets that jointly cover political attitudes, voting intentions, actual electoral behavior, candidate evaluations, issue positions, political communication, and sociodemographic characteristics. The collection also supports comparisons between the 2009, 2013, and 2017 federal elections."},{"title":"German State Election Surveys – GESIS Election Studies Collection","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/elections/german-state-elections","justification":"Relevant resource for locating representative election surveys conducted around German state elections, including studies from the 2010s. The collection contains surveys associated with state electoral contests and provides opportunities to examine political attitudes, voting intentions, party preferences, and regional electoral behavior. Particularly useful for extending research beyond the 2013 federal election to regional political contexts and investigating relationships between federal and state party competition. The GESIS collection includes the 2013 Bavarian election tracking study and historical state-election survey data."},{"title":"Politbarometer – German Political Opinion and Election Survey Data","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/elections","justification":"Valuable complementary source for investigating German public opinion and electoral preferences during the 2010s, including the 2013 federal election period. The Politbarometer survey series, conducted by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen and archived by GESIS, provides repeated measurements of political opinions and attitudes. Its annual cumulative datasets support longitudinal analysis of changes in public opinion and political preferences. Particularly useful for contextualizing GLES findings within broader trends in German electoral politics and comparing attitudes across multiple election periods."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study – Election Research Data and Documentation","url_or_doi":"https://gles.eu/daten/","justification":"Dedicated GLES data access resource identified by the WZB Berlin Social Science Center. It provides access to research data and documentation covering German federal elections beginning in 2009, including the 2013 election. The available study types include election campaign panels, rolling cross-sectional surveys, long-term tracking studies, candidate surveys, media content data, and election-related cross-sections. Particularly valuable for researchers seeking multiple complementary sources on voting behavior, campaign communication, political attitudes, party evaluations, and media effects during the 2013 election campaign."}]}
